script: I took $400, lied about a wallet—what happened next shocked me.. I was standing in the grocery store parking lot, scrolling through my phone, when I spotted a wallet on the asphalt. Inside: a driver's license, a handful of credit cards, and about $400 in cash. I didn't even think about the owner. I grabbed the cash. (Micro‑hook: "I grabbed the cash, like, because I could.") Then I walked up to customer service and said, "Hey, I found a wallet—no cash in it." I was basically saying, "I am not a thief, I am a good Samaritan." A few minutes later, an employee called the owner and told him, "We found his wallet." I just stood there, listening, feeling like a genius. The owner got his ID and cards back, so in my head I was like, "This isn't stealing, it's a loophole." I kept repeating that to keep the guilt from creeping in. The owner came out, relief plastered on his face. He thanked everyone, apologized for the hassle, and said he was worried because rent was due that week. I just walked away before he could even see my face. (Micro‑hook: "I walked away before he could see my face.") That scene is still a punch in the gut. I didn't need that money; I just pretended I did to justify a crime against someone already having a rough week. I hid behind a technical excuse to sleep better at night. Looking back, I wasn't clever. I was just a thief who got lucky. I stole from someone in distress, and now I am the one who can't shake the feeling that I am not as great as I thought.
